title.narrative: Third Basic Education Quality Improvement Project

description.narrative: The objective of the Third Basic Education Quality Improvement Project is to increase equity, quality, and efficiency in providing preschool and primary education. There are two project components. The first comprises several subcomponents, including expanding the existing pedagogical model of urban, full-time schools and adapting the urban full-time school model to rural areas; constructing, transforming, rehabilitating, and equipping full-time schools as well as financing civil works and the acquisition and distribution of furniture and kitchen equipment; acquiring school equipment, learning materials, and school libraries; teacher training on the full-time school model, and providing new education technologies and bilingual education; and strengthening the partnership between schools and parents. The second component finances institutional strengthening of the overall education system, including reforming teacher training, and developing and implementing Education Improvement Projects (PMEs) as well as developing a research and evaluation division, implementing a management information system, and project administration.

Improve the quality of preschool and primary education (ages 4-11): academic achievement in Mathematics

comment.narrative: Indicator is the percentage of students achieving a passing score in the primary education grade being tested.

In 2005 the ANEP changed the methodology to measure this indicator from the Classic Test Theory to the Item Response Theory. TheBorrower and the Bank agreed to prepare a study to define an equivalence of the levels of achievement of passing scores between thetwo methodologies. The results of this study are expected to be ready for Q4 of CY2012.

During the mission the government explained that the total student places are in fact 45,199. The difference between the installedcapacity and the real number of students is linked to the fact that the national guidelines for school organization changed in2011,reducing students per classroom from 30 to 25.
